data.title: Wolters Kluwer launches Blue Chip IQ, bringing AI to decades of trusted economic intelligence
data.description:
Wolters Kluwer launches Blue Chip IQ, bringing AI to decades of trusted economic intelligence

New AI-powered experience enables decision-makers to explore historical forecasts and uncover economic insights faster

Wolters Kluwer’s Legal & Regulatory U.S. business today announced the launch of Blue Chip IQ, a new AI-powered economic intelligence experience. Economists and decision-makers can leverage the power of AI to engage directly with the authoritative consensus forecasts, historical data, and expert commentary found in the company’s renowned Blue Chip Economic Indicators® and Blue Chip Financial Forecasts® publications.

“The Blue Chip forecasts have long served as a weathervane for decision-makers around the world,” said Chris Carr, Portfolio Director for the Blue Chip publications. “With Blue Chip IQ, we’re helping those same leaders dive even further into decades of trusted consensus forecasts and economic intelligence to navigate shifting expectations with confidence.”

Blue Chip IQ combines responsible AI with the trusted forecasts, historical data and expert analysis that have defined the Blue Chip franchise for decades, including commentary produced through Wolters Kluwer's long-standing relationship with Haver Analytics.

  • AI-powered conversational discovery: Users can swiftly elevate historical context and identify long-term trends by using AI-powered chat functionality to surface relevant insights from years of Blue Chip forecasts and analysis.
  • Dynamic data exploration: Trusted economic data can be sorted by panelist, variable and time period to more easily trace the evolution of consensus expectations over time. Consensus and individual forecasts can also be quickly compared to identify potential outliers.
  • Interactive visualization: Users can build custom charts to visualize complex economic data and forecast trends, providing accessible visuals for analysis, presentations and executive decision-making.
  • Connected data and expert analysis: The ability to seamlessly move between quantitative forecasts and the expert commentary behind them allow for a richer understanding of the forces shifting the economic outlook.

With a history dating back to 1976, Blue Chip Economic Indicators® and Blue Chip Financial Forecasts are trusted sources of economic forecasting that bring together consensus views from leading economists. The publications' expert analysis is supported by a long-standing editorial relationship with Haver Analytics, a respected provider of economic data and research.

Wolters Kluwer’s Legal & Regulatory division enables legal and compliance professionals to improve productivity and performance, mitigate risk, and solve complex problems with confidence. Its expert solutions combine deep domain knowledge with advanced technology and services to deliver better outcomes, advanced analytics, and improved productivity for customers.

About Wolters Kluwer

Wolters Kluwer (EURONEXT: WKL) is a global leader in information solutions, software and services for professionals in healthcare; tax and accounting; financial and corporate compliance; legal and regulatory; corporate performance and ESG. We help our customers make critical decisions every day by providing expert solutions that combine deep domain knowledge with technology and services. Wolters Kluwer reported 2025 annual revenues of €6.1 billion. The group serves customers in over 180 countries, maintains operations in over 40 countries, and employs approximately 21,100 people worldwide. The company is headquartered in Alphen aan den Rijn, the Netherlands.

Wolters Kluwer shares are listed on Euronext Amsterdam (WKL) and are included in the AEX and Euronext 100 indices. Wolters Kluwer has a sponsored Level 1 American Depositary Receipt (ADR) program. The ADRs are traded on the over-the-counter market in the U.S. (WTKWY).

For more information, visit www.wolterskluwer.com, follow us on LinkedIn, Facebook, YouTube and Instagram.

data.title: North Star Carbon Removal Project Selected by Government of Canada for Landmark Carbon Removal Procurement Program
data.description:
North Star Carbon Removal Project Selected by Government of Canada for Landmark Carbon Removal Procurement Program

  • Microsoft-backed Saskatchewan project developed by MLTC and Svante among only three BECCS projects selected

North Star, a planned large-scale carbon dioxide removal (CDR) project being developed by Meadow Lake Tribal Council (MLTC) and Svante Technologies Inc. (Svante), has been selected by the Government of Canada as a qualified supplier under the federal Request for Standing Offer (RFSO) for the Acquisition and Retirement of Credits from Carbon Dioxide Removal Projects.

This press release features multimedia. View the full release here: https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20261118228180/en/

The proposed North Star bioenergy with carbon capture and storage project is being developed by the Meadow Lake Tribal Council (MLTC) and Svante. The project will generate durable carbon dioxide removal credits by capturing biogenic CO2 from the MLTC Bioenergy Center in Meadow Lake, SK, Canada, and storing it deep underground in a geological storage site.

North Star was one of only three bioenergy with carbon capture and storage (BECCS) projects selected through the competitive process, following a rigorous evaluation of technical, commercial, and procurement requirements. The selection establishes North Star as an eligible supplier for future annual federal purchases of high-quality carbon removal credits.

"This announcement marks an important step forward for Canada's carbon removal industry," said Claude Letourneau, President and CEO of Svante. "Creating reliable demand for carbon dioxide removal credits helps unlock investment, accelerate project development, and strengthen Canada's position in a rapidly growing global carbon market. Over time, carbon removals have the potential to become a strategic Canadian international export under the Paris Agreement Article 6.0 framework, generating economic value through investment and job creation, while helping organizations at home and abroad achieve their climate goals."

Located in Meadow Lake, Saskatchewan, North Star is being developed to convert sustainably sourced forestry residuals into clean energy while permanently capturing and storing biogenic carbon dioxide. The project is expected to generate durable carbon removal credits while creating economic opportunities for Indigenous communities and the broader region.

"This recognition reinforces the strength of the vision behind North Star," said Chief Jeremy Norman, Tribal Chief of MLTC. "Our Nations have long understood the importance of responsible stewardship of the land and its resources. Through North Star, we have an opportunity to create jobs, attract investment, and build an Indigenous-led economic opportunity that delivers lasting benefits for our communities while contributing to Canada's climate goals."

North Star has also secured a long-term carbon removal offtake agreement with Microsoft, positioning it among Canada's most advanced planned carbon removal projects. Beyond the voluntary carbon market, the Government of Canada’s procurement program is designed to create demand for high-quality carbon removals while helping the federal government advance climate objectives. As one of the county’s first initiatives of its kind, it represents an important step toward building a robust domestic market for engineered carbon removal.

About North Star

North Star is a planned bioenergy with carbon capture and storage (BECCS) project being developed in Meadow Lake, Saskatchewan, Canada. By utilizing sustainably sourced forestry residuals from the MLTC Bioenergy Centre to produce energy while permanently removing carbon dioxide from the atmosphere, North Star aims to deliver durable carbon removals, support Indigenous economic participation, and contribute to Canada's climate and economic objectives.

About MLTC

MLTC was formed in 1981 and represents nine First Nations located in Northwest Saskatchewan. MLTC invests in businesses to meaningfully participate in Saskatchewan's economy, supporting economic reconciliation in a rural and remote area of the province. 100% of the distributions flow to the nine First Nations, to foster local economic growth; enhance on-reserve education; healthcare; youth and elder programs; housing; and other community social and infrastructure needs.

About Svante

Svante is an integrated carbon management company headquartered in Vancouver, Canada. The company makes nanoengineered filters and modular rotating contactor machines that capture and remove CO2 in an environmentally responsible way from industrial emissions and the air. The company manufactures filters for direct air capture and develops carbon capture and storage projects from source to sink. Svante is on Fast Company’s 2026 World Changing Idea’s list, the Global Cleantech 100 Hall of Fame and TIME & Statista’s list of Top Greentech Companies of 2025. For more information, visit www.svanteinc.com.

data.title: Xsolla Gives Games a New Home for Their Players on Desktop and the Web, With Rewards to Help Bring Players Back
data.description:
Xsolla Gives Games a New Home for Their Players on Desktop and the Web, With Rewards to Help Bring Players Back

Developers Can Now Reach Players on Desktop and the Web With Xsolla Player and Xsolla Pages

Xsolla (USA), Inc., a global commerce company, is giving game developers two new capabilities designed to reach players and encourage repeat engagement. Xsolla Player and Xsolla Pages are now available, letting developers integrate quests, rewards, and partner-funded offers into the player flow.

This press release features multimedia. View the full release here: https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20261119175727/en/

Graphic: Xsolla

Xsolla Player is a desktop app that players install once and access with their Xsolla ID, bringing their game library and inventory together without separate sign-ups for each game.

Xsolla Pages creates search-optimized storefronts on the web for every title in a developer’s catalog, with direct checkout.

PC studios work hard to win a player's first click, then work just as hard for every session after. Bringing players back is a challenge and has traditionally required paying to reach them again. Meanwhile, direct web sales have become a major revenue channel. Still, building and maintaining a separate web store or another app placement for every title is not practical for many studios, especially those with large back catalogs.

“A game shouldn’t only exist where a studio pays to reach players,” said Chris Hewish, President of Xsolla (USA), Inc. “Xsolla Player and Xsolla Pages put it on two more platforms, with quests, rewards, and offers giving players more ways to engage. Anyone can build a web page. What's hard is knowing which partner makes sense for a game and which offer fits each market. Xsolla Player and Xsolla Pages help studios with that.”

With Xsolla Player, gamers browse PC, web, and cloud games, start them with one click, and see live quests that highlight what to play next. Rewards are available for activities such as signing in, completing onboarding, launching a game for the first time, and finishing quests, and studios can also add their own quests and return-to-play rewards. Eligible items land in the player’s Backpack and carry over from one session to the next, while games and their available offers remain visible as players browse other titles.

Xsolla Pages gives each game a storefront on the web without the overhead of building one. Pages are built from a studio's existing catalog, and developers decide what each one sells, how it looks, and which markets it serves. Every page includes:

  • Search-ready setup. Search tags and social previews are set up, and page speed is checked, before each page goes live.
  • Backpack rewards. In-game items and perks that players keep in their Backpack, subject to the game’s terms, and use in-game.
  • Direct checkout. Purchases run on Xsolla's Merchant of Record infrastructure across 200+ geographies, with access to 1,000+ local payment methods and support for local payment and tax requirements.

Xsolla Pages is available to developers of any size, from studios with a single game to publishers with thousands of titles, for new releases and back catalog alike. More than 1,500 game teams already work with Xsolla.

Studios can learn more about Xsolla Player and get started with Xsolla Pages.

Readers can also complete a short Xsolla Quest at: xsolla.pro/p3-quest

What is Xsolla Quest? Xsolla Quest lets people complete a few simple steps on an Xsolla page to receive an item.

About Xsolla

Xsolla (USA), Inc. is a global commerce company that builds and provides all the things developers need to launch, grow, and monetize video games. Headquartered in Los Angeles, California, the company supports studios of every size, from indie to AAA, with solutions across direct-to-consumer commerce, intelligent payments, entertainment-based IP, and player engagement products. Xsolla helps developers fund, distribute, market, and monetize their games at scale. Trusted by more than 70% of the top 100 highest-grossing games, Xsolla operates as the merchant of record across 200+ geographies with access to 1,000+ local payment methods worldwide. Grounded in a deep belief in the future of video games, Xsolla is resolute in bringing opportunities together and unlocking growth for creators everywhere.

For more information, visit xsolla.com.

Xsolla Player and Xsolla Pages are offered by Xsolla (USA), Inc. (“Xsolla”). Rewards, in-game currency, badges, and Xsolla Points have no cash value and cannot be exchanged for cash or cryptocurrency. In-game currency can be used only as permitted by the game that issues it. Partner-funded offers, including any cashback or installment plans, are provided by third parties and subject to their terms. Rewards and offers are available only in supported territories.

data.title: AM Best Revises Issuer Credit Rating Outlook to Negative for Courtesy Insurance Company
data.description:
AM Best Revises Issuer Credit Rating Outlook to Negative for Courtesy Insurance Company

AM Best has revised the outlook to negative from stable for the Long-Term Issuer Credit Rating (Long-Term ICR) and affirmed the Financial Strength Rating (FSR) of A (Excellent) and the Long-Term ICR of “a+” (Excellent) of Courtesy Insurance Company (Courtesy) (Deerfield Beach, FL). The outlook of the FSR is stable.

The Credit Ratings (ratings) reflect Courtesy’s balance sheet strength, which AM Best assesses as very strong, as well as its strong operating performance, neutral business profile and appropriate enterprise risk management (ERM).

The revision of the Long-Term ICR outlook to negative from stable reflects Courtesy’s operating performance metrics compared with its peer companies. The company has reported underwriting losses in each of the past three years due to macro-economic factors and supply chain disruptions along with parts and labor inflation. These factors, which have driven elevated loss costs, are expected to persist over the short-medium term for Courtesy and firms within the vehicle service contract sector. The group has reported underwriting metrics that compare unfavorably to similarly assessed peers at the strong assessment level. Management has implemented mitigation initiatives that are expected to improve results over the medium-to-long term.

Courtesy’s balance sheet strength remains very strong with supportive risk-adjusted capitalization, enhanced financial flexibility and consistent surplus growth. Courtesy is an integral part of the group’s strategy and benefits from lift afforded by its ultimate parent, JM Family Enterprises, Inc., in the form of implicit and explicit support, which is evident from past capital contributions. The company’s business profile is assessed as neutral given the significant and wide reach provided by affiliates within the organization. The ERM assessment is appropriate for the size and the scope of Courtesy’s operations.

Negative rating action could occur if underwriting metrics continue to trend unfavorably compared with similarly assessed warranty composite peers. Negative rating action may also occur if there is a change in the financial condition of the ultimate parent or if Courtesy’s strategic role within the group materially changes.

This press release relates to Credit Ratings that have been published on AM Best’s website. For all rating information relating to the release and pertinent disclosures, including details of the office responsible for issuing each of the individual ratings referenced in this release, please see AM Best’s Recent Rating Activity web page. For additional information regarding the use and limitations of Credit Rating opinions, please view Guide to Best's Credit Ratings. For information on the proper use of Best’s Credit Ratings, Best’s Performance Assessments, Best’s Preliminary Credit Assessments and AM Best press releases, please view Guide to Proper Use of Best’s Ratings & Assessments.

AM Best is a global credit rating agency, news publisher and data analytics provider specializing in the insurance industry. data.title: Tashkent Content Market to launch in February 2027
data.description:
Tashkent Content Market to launch in February 2027

Tashkent Content Market to launch in February 2027

PR Newswire

TASHKENT, Uzbekistan, Nov. 19, 2026

New international marketplace will connect content producers with buyers, distributors and co-production partners

TASHKENT, Uzbekistan, Nov. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- The inaugural Tashkent Content Market (TCM 2027) will take place on February 4-5, 2027, at Uzexpocentre, bringing together audiovisual content producers and international buyers to explore licensing, distribution and co-production opportunities.

The event is organized by the Centre for the Production of Content for the Mass Media under the Administration of the President of the Republic of Uzbekistan, together with international and regional partner organizations.

Organizers expect more than 3,000 participants from over 50 countries, with more than 100 exhibition stands across two pavilions covering 5,500 square meters. Participants will include producers, broadcasters, distributors, streaming platforms, rights holders, investors and technology companies.

Under the theme "From the Silk Road to the Global Content Market," TCM 2027 aims to expand international opportunities for Uzbekistan's content industry and support Tashkent's development as a regional media hub. Its priorities include promoting content exports, connecting local producers with international buyers, supporting co-productions, and attracting investment in media and technology projects.

The two-day program will combine an international exhibition with scheduled business-to-business meetings, industry discussions, professional screenings, master classes and networking activities. Producers and rights holders will present catalogs, new projects and licensing offers spanning films, documentaries, television series, animation, television formats and digital content.

A dedicated online participant platform will help companies identify potential partners, arrange meetings in advance and manage personal schedules. Registration will be available in four languages.

Industry sessions will address content monetization, artificial intelligence in production and distribution, and international licensing. Screenings and master classes will introduce projects to professional audiences and provide opportunities to exchange experience with industry experts.

The market will also provide a setting for negotiating and signing licensing, distribution and co-production agreements, while networking activities will connect established professionals with emerging creators.

Further information about participation and the event program is available at www.tcm.uz.

About Tashkent Content Market

Tashkent Content Market is an international platform for showcasing, buying, selling and licensing audiovisual content, developing distribution partnerships and supporting co-production projects.

data.title: Evonik Shares Tumble After BASF Ends Takeover Efforts
data.description:
By Sarah Sloat

Shares in Evonik tumbled after German chemicals company BASF said it dropped its efforts to acquire the company.

The stock fell 15% to 18.51 euros.

BASF said the decision followed Evonik's rejection of two offers.

"Despite the indication that BASF was prepared to consider a further moderate increase to its offer, the Executive Board of Evonik has not shown meaningful engagement until today," BASF said in a statement.

BASF also said that an assessment of Evonik's standalone prospects and risks didn't justify a higher valuation.

"Against this background, BASF does not consider it to be in the best interests of its shareholders to pursue the transaction at a higher price," BASF said.

data.title: Ron Johnson's Social Security gaffe buried important news
data.description:
By Brett Arends

Wisconsin Republican's remarks overshadowed what might have been a useful Senate committee hearing about fixing Social Security

Sen. Ron Johnson's gaffe about shutting down Social Security drowned out the latest Senate deliberations on the subject.

Spare a thought for Ron Johnson.

The Republican senator from Wisconsin is suffering from "Long Ayn Rand." He was exposed to the famous author's radical right-wing ideas when he was younger, and sadly he's never recovered.

Johnson, who called Rand's tedious, doorstopping allegory "Atlas Shrugged" his "foundational book," just suffered a serious Long Ayn Rand relapse live on TV. It caused him to stick both feet in his mouth and denounce Social Security as a "Ponzi" scheme that should be "shut down."

Many people catch Ayn Rand disease (or the left-wing version, Karl Marx disease) when they are young. Most grow out of it by their early 20s. A few, tragically, have the chronic condition for life. There is no cure.

(Among others tragically affected by Long Ayn Rand was the novelist's friend, the late Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan, whose condition led him to a series of spectacular blunders.)

It was a shame that Johnson suffered his LAR relapse on TV because it overshadowed what might otherwise have been a useful Senate committee hearing about how to fix, or rescue, Social Security. Democratic committee colleagues of Johnson's spent most of a 90-minute hearing on Social Security quoting the Republican's gaffe in various tones of fury and disbelief. Johnson repeatedly had to argue that he had misspoken, or spoken poorly, and that he didn't want to shut down Social Security. He said that he was proposing a bill to make sure benefits are never cut, no matter what happens to the trust fund.

It was all pointless.

It is not my job to defend or explain U.S. senators when they say or do stupid things in public. But buried under Johnson's gaffe were some useful points that ought to be widely understood - no matter where you are politically. They are essential to understanding the crisis facing Social Security, and any proposals to shore up its finances.

The first is that almost nobody - including Johnson - is proposing cutting Social Security benefits from current levels. The most conservative, right-wing proposals being put forward consist of scaling back future benefit increases so that they are only in line with inflation. So someone retiring in 20 or 30 years would get the same benefit - in constant dollars - as someone retiring today. (These are proposals to avoid the current situation, which would cause deep, automatic cuts in six or eight years' time. Everyone admits this would be a disaster, and everyone wants to avoid it.)

This is exactly the idea recently put forward by John Cogan, a fellow at Stanford University's conservative Hoover Institution. He proposes limiting the growth of average Social Security benefits per person to match economywide inflation, and calls for the growth of Medicare and other federal medical benefits to match specific healthcare inflation.

"Limiting the growth in cash entitlement benefits per recipient to consumer price inflation and the growth in healthcare entitlement spending per recipient to the growth in economywide healthcare costs would restrain the growth in federal spending to 2.9 percent per year," he writes. "The spending limitation would reduce the budget deficit by two-thirds in 15 years and balance the budget in 20 years," he adds.

To be clear, I am neither endorsing (nor critiquing) Cogan's proposal. And you can certainly challenge some of his mathematical and economic assumptions. But the general point is important: Among responsible or respected analysts, even the very conservative are not talking seriously about cutting Social Security benefits from today's levels. And, maybe more important, the expected costs of future benefits growth are so big that simply freezing benefits in real terms - in other words, raising them no more than inflation in future years - can have a huge impact on the budget math.

Would this be a "cut?" Yes and no. On one level, obviously, keeping benefits the same in real terms is not a cut compared with today. But it would be a cut compared with what is currently projected.

It is little understood, but Social Security contains a built-in escalator that gives every cohort of retirees per year, even adjusted for inflation, more than their predecessors. This is in addition to the annual cost-of-living adjustment, or COLA, which all beneficiaries receive every year. It applies to your initial benefits and is based on something called "average wage indexing." It was introduced in the 1970s. It means every cohort gets a raise compared with the one before. But if we give every new retiree more than predecessors, while the number of retirees is also ballooning, and retirees are living much longer than before, that raises obvious mathematical issues.

Johnson's other reasonable point is that the so-called Social Security trust fund is a fiction. There is no fund. There is no lockbox. The so-called assets owned by the fund are simply accounting entries, whereby the federal government promises to pay future benefits out of general taxation or borrowing. So retirees aren't "getting their own money back." Their Social Security payroll taxes went to pay the benefits of their parents' and grandparents' generations. When they retire, their benefits will be paid by their children and grandchildren.

The thing about Social Security reform that everyone should remember is that multiple things are true at the same time. Many of the Democratic talking points are perfectly true. So are many of the Republican talking points. It's often not either-or. It's and ... and ... and ...

The best comment of the day came from Virginia Democrat Mark Warner. He pointed out that fixing Social Security was really just a question of math: raising program revenues and slowing the growth of future costs. "To say we can't fix this is outrageous," he said. "It is eminently fixable. This is math. It isn't policy changes. It's math."

Quite so.

-Brett Arends

data.title: Investors are rushing back into cybersecurity stocks after a string of outages. Here's what to know before buying.
data.description:
By Christine Idzelis and Philip van Doorn

The theme is increasingly attractive to investors, and Wall Street has taken notice

Cybersecurity is "rapidly moving up the investment agenda," Barclays analysts said.

Investors are buying the latest dip in cybersecurity stocks as a number of widespread outages in recent days have stoked fears about the threat of hacking enabled by artificial intelligence.

Cybersecurity stocks were swept up in a broad-based tech selloff earlier this month, but they have rebounded as pressure on the broader AI trade has eased. The fact that a spate of recent outages have grabbed the public's attention has not been lost on Wall Street.

"Cybersecurity is rapidly moving up the investment agenda as attacks become more frequent and far-reaching," Barclays analysts wrote in a report shared with MarketWatch.

The Wall Street Journal reported that a string of recent outages at airports and banks and in Microsoft's popular 365 enterprise software suite were caused by software updates gone wrong. An analysis from Connecticut-based hedge fund Bridgewater Associates found that the number of reported cybersecurity incidents had increased exponentially in recent months.

Growth industry with defensive characteristics

Cybersecurity stocks are compelling because they offer investors a helpful mix of characteristics. It's a growth industry that is also inherently defensive in nature. Companies will likely need to steadily increase their spending on cybersecurity as AI drives more hacking attempts, Christian Magoon, chief executive of Amplify ETFs, told MarketWatch in an interview.

In a sense, they're a little bit like a utility, Magoon said: "It is essential spending."

And the threat to physical infrastructure is growing increasingly imminent, Barclays warned.

"Cybersecurity is no longer primarily about protecting personal data or defending against ransomware - attacks are increasingly reaching into physical infrastructure, supply chains and essential services, creating more direct consequences for business continuity and the physical economy," the Barclays analysts wrote.

Attention on the space started to pick up even earlier, after a series of cyberattacks rattled Europe. In October, "hackers remotely manipulated connected refrigeration systems" across 700 French supermarkets, the Barclays analysts said, "forcing stores to discard food."

Buying the dip

Investors appear to be stepping up to buy the recent pullback. Cybersecurity exchange-traded funds listed in the U.S. have seen about $115 million of inflows in the past week, bringing their total this year to almost $3.4 billion, according to FactSet data through Wednesday. Palo Alto Networks shares (PANW) were up nearly 10% ahead of the opening bell on Thursday after a strong earnings report.

The reaction offered a stark contrast with what followed Fortinet's (FTNT) quarterly earnings released late last month.

The table below compares November performance with the 2026 total return for a handful of the most popular cybersecurity ETFs.

Although the ETFs' forward P/E valuations are down significantly since the end of October, strong 2026 performance has kept them on an upward trend.
